title: Pythagoras' Theorem
seo_title: Pythagoras' Theorem – JSS 2 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Use Pythagoras' theorem to find the hypotenuse and the shorter sides of right-angled triangles; test whether a triangle is right-angled. (summary of the NERDC JSS 2 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free JSS 2 maths worksheets on Pythagoras' theorem: finding the hypotenuse, finding a shorter side, answers to decimal places and testing for a right angle. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: c is the hypotenuse, opposite the right angle.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • In a right-angled triangle, the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides: c² = a² + b².
  • To find a shorter side, subtract: a² = c² − b².
  • If a² + b² = c² for three sides, the triangle has a right angle. 3, 4, 5 and 5, 12, 13 are Pythagorean triples.

Examples

Example

Legs 6 cm and 8 cm

36 + 64 = 100

Answer: 10 cm

Example

Hypotenuse 13 m, one side 5 m

169 − 25 = 144

Answer: 12 m

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Adding to find a shorter sideSubtract from c².
Forgetting the square rootc² = 100 means c = 10.
Using the wrong side as cc is opposite the right angle.
